title: Philippine digital participation is exposed to widespread cyber incidents while awareness and reporting remain low
source_unit: Philippine Statistics Authority, 2024 National Information and Communications Technology Household Survey: cybersecurity and data privacy awareness, incidents, and reporting
geography: Philippines; individuals aged 10 years and over and ICT-device users across regions

denominator.unit: estimated individuals aged 10 years and over represented by the NICTHS

cybersecurity_data_privacy_awareness.unit: percent of individuals aged 10 years and over aware of cybersecurity and data privacy

urban_awareness.unit: percent of urban individuals aged 10 years and over aware

rural_awareness.unit: percent of rural individuals aged 10 years and over aware

tertiary_education_awareness.unit: percent of individuals with tertiary education aware

primary_or_lower_awareness.unit: percent of individuals with primary education or lower aware

ncr_awareness.unit: percent of individuals in the National Capital Region aware

barmm_awareness.unit: percent of individuals in Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao aware

mechanism.value: Digital participation can expand faster than the ability to recognize privacy and cyber risk, with awareness sharply stratified by education and place

observations.method: NICTHS 2024 cybersecurity and data privacy module measuring self-reported awareness among individuals aged 10 years and over, with education, urban-rural, and regional breakdowns.
observations.uncertainty: Awareness is self-reported and does not test knowledge, protective behavior, causal risk reduction, or whether respondents interpret cybersecurity and data privacy consistently.
observations.subgroup: Philippine individuals aged 10 years and over, with subgroup definitions specified by the source.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher awareness may reflect education, occupation, institutional exposure, or survey response differences rather than greater objective protection; lower awareness does not prove higher incident risk.

denominator.unit: estimated individuals aged 10 years and over who used an ICT device

any_cybersecurity_incident.unit: percent of ICT-device users experiencing at least one cybersecurity incident

approximate_incident_affected.unit: estimated individuals experiencing at least one cybersecurity incident

urban_incident.unit: percent of urban ICT-device users experiencing an incident

rural_incident.unit: percent of rural ICT-device users experiencing an incident

tertiary_education_incident.unit: percent of ICT-device users with tertiary education experiencing an incident

primary_or_lower_incident.unit: percent of ICT-device users with primary education or lower experiencing an incident

reported_to_authorities.unit: percent of incident victims reporting incidents to authorities

mechanism.value: Cyber incident exposure is widespread among ICT-device users, but formal recourse is thin, leaving digital participation with a large unaddressed trust and protection burden

observations.method: NICTHS 2024 cybersecurity module measuring self-reported technology-enabled incidents among ICT-device users and reporting behavior among incident victims.
observations.uncertainty: The incident category is survey-defined and self-reported rather than forensic; the approximate affected count is derived from the source's reported denominator and share, and the reporting share uses the source's victim denominator.
observations.subgroup: Philippine ICT-device users aged 10 years and over and their reported incident experiences.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported incident need not imply financial loss, persistent harm, or failed platform security, while low reporting may reflect informal resolution, uncertainty about where to report, or low perceived benefit rather than absence of concern.

denominator.unit: estimated individuals experiencing at least one cybersecurity incident; source estimate

sms_fraud_among_victims.unit: percent of incident victims experiencing SMS fraud

hacking_among_victims.unit: percent of incident victims experiencing hacking

phishing_among_victims.unit: percent of incident victims experiencing phishing

cyberbullying_libel_among_victims.unit: percent of incident victims experiencing cyberbullying or libel

barmm_sms_fraud.unit: percent of incident victims in Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao experiencing SMS fraud

ilocos_sms_fraud.unit: percent of incident victims in Ilocos experiencing SMS fraud

barmm_phishing.unit: percent of incident victims in Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao experiencing phishing

mechanism.value: SMS fraud dominates the mobile-first risk surface, while regional patterns differ enough that a single national digital-risk profile obscures localized exposure

observations.method: NICTHS 2024 cybersecurity module measuring reported incident types among victims, including regional breakdowns.
observations.uncertainty: The source's incident-type percentages may reflect multiple experiences or source-specific response rules; they are not verified case counts, monetary-loss shares, or estimates of platform liability.
observations.subgroup: Philippine cybersecurity-incident victims aged 10 years and over, with regional subgroup definitions specified by the source.
observations.counterinterpretation: SMS fraud prevalence may reflect higher recognition or reporting of familiar messages rather than greater underlying incidence; regional differences may partly reflect device, language, network, or survey-context differences.

related_sources.claim: Official PSA NICTHS release page reports cybersecurity and data privacy awareness, incident exposure, incident types, regional differences, and reporting to authorities.
PSA statistical-tables page identifies the NICTHS data products and related ICT household tables.

boundary: This record adds Philippine evidence on cybersecurity and data privacy awareness, incident exposure, fraud modality, regional variation, and reporting behavior. It does not measure forensic incident counts, financial loss, causal risk, platform liability, institutional response quality, or the welfare effect of digital participation.
